thread:
anya: quick eyeball please — I'm landing a tf change that deploys external-secrets via helm into prod and wires up IRSA + a kms grant. want to make sure i'm not missing a principal/condition weirdness. pasted below.

anya: terraform snippet I'm planning to apply:
```hcl
resource \"aws_iam_role\" \"external_secrets_irsa\" {
  name = \"es-helm-irsa-prod\"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa_assume.json
}

resource \"aws_kms_grant\" \"es_kms_grant\" {
  key_id = aws_kms_key.data_key.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.external_secrets_irsa.arn
  operations = [\"Decrypt\", \"GenerateDataKey\"]
}
```

anya: helm values for the chart (pod annotation):
```yaml
serviceAccount:
  create: false
  name: external-secrets
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/es-helm-irsa-prod
```

anya: question: is using aws_kms_grant with grantee_principal=role ARN reliable here, or should I instead modify the key policy to allow the OIDC principal (sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity) with kms:ViaService or specific conditions?

micah: short answer: grants are ok for short-lived permissions but grants don't survive key rotation if you re-create keys. also grants are tied to principal ARNs — ok for role.

micah: note: if external-secrets runs as a role that assumes via IRSA, the effective principal doing Decrypt is the role ARN, so grantee_principal should work. add kms:ViaService condition if you want to restrict to eks.amazonaws.com.

sam: add to that: terraform's aws_kms_grant can be tricky in TF plans if the role changes name/arn. we prefer key policy statements for long-lived service integrations. grants are great for short-term automation.

anya: got it. i was mostly worried about the cross-account backup KMS key we use for snapshots — that key is in a different acct (backup acct). i was trying to issue a grant from our prod acct to the role in the app acct.

micah: cross-account grants are allowed but both accounts need proper policies. For cross-account, the grantee_principal must be the IAM ARN in the grantee account. Also check key policy principal for aws:PrincipalOrgID or explicit principals.

devex: small gotcha we hit before: when using IRSA, the session name that sts issues can be long. If you have key policy conditions on kms:EncryptionContext:aws:sts:caller or on kms:viaService, make sure they don't break due to session name length. Not common but seen.

anya: terraform-bot: plan ran in CI and flagged a drift: 
terraform-bot: \"Warning: aws_kms_grant conflicts with existing key policy statement granting similar permissions\" (automated)

anya: hmm. I did try to add a key statement to the backup key that allows the role across accounts to decrypt, but CI says there's a conflict.

micah: you probably have a broad key policy allowing the whole account to use the key. When a grant attempts to add explicit permissions for the same principal, KMS will accept it but Terraform warns. Two approaches:
- update key policy to be the single source of truth (recommended for cross-account long-lived access)
- keep grants but suppress the TF warning and document lifecycle (less ideal)

sam: for Helm/external-secrets specifically, we also added an option to use envelope encryption with a KMS key in the same account and then replicate backups. That avoids cross-account grants entirely. Might be a simpler migration path.

anya: ok leaning toward updating key_policy on backup key to add the role ARN from the prod account. any suggested policy snippet?

micah: something like:
```json
{
  \"Sid\": \"AllowExternalSecretsRoleDecrypt\",
  \"Effect\": \"Allow\",
  \"Principal\": {\"AWS\": \"arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/es-helm-irsa-prod\"},
  \"Action\": [\"kms:Decrypt\", \"kms:GenerateDataKey\"],
  \"Resource\": \"*\",
  \"Condition\": {\"StringEquals\": {\"kms:ViaService\": \"eks.us-west-2.amazonaws.com\"}}
}
```

micah: tweak region/service as needed. Condition is optional but good to restrict to EKS.

devex: small add: in our org we prefer using aws:SourceAccount + kms:ViaService to avoid principal spoofing. e.g., put SourceAccount = 123456789012 and ViaService = eks.us-west-2.amazonaws.com.

anya: thanks. final q: do I need an explicit trust relationship for the role so that the service account annotation can assume it? my assume_policy currently uses the OIDC provider sub and a condition on StringEquals: {\"sts:aud\": \"sts.amazonaws.com\"} — is that sufficient?

micah: yes that's standard. ensure the OIDC provider ARN in the policy is correct and the sub matches serviceaccount:namespace:name. Example assume policy block: 
```json
{\"Effect\":\"Allow\",\"Principal\":{\"Federated\":\"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:oidc-provider/oidc.eks.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/id/EXAMPLE\"},\"Action\":\"sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity\",\"Condition\":{\"StringEquals\":{\"oidc.eks.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/id/EXAMPLE:sub\":\"system:serviceaccount:external-secrets:external-secrets\"}}}
```

sam: also audit the service account name in helm values — sometimes charts use a generated name or a different SA. if create:false and name matches, good.

anya: perfect — i'll switch to key policy change for the backup key, add ViaService+SourceAccount conditions, and leave the grant in our prod acct for now as a short-term stopgap. will open a follow-up PR to remove the grant after we verify.

micah: :thumbsup:

devex: ping me when the PR's ready and i'll add a short runbook for rollback.

anya: thanks all, will update PR and tag you.
